featured_reviews.review_text:
Every student has a different perspective about college. What may seem bad to one student might be perfectly fine for another. However, as a recent 12th pass-out who studied at Tolani College during both 11th and 12th grade, I can confidently say that my experience was excellent.

If you are genuinely interested in studies and willing to learn, Tolani College is one of the best places you can choose. The quality of teaching is impressive and, in my opinion, often better than many coaching classes that charge several times more than the college fees.

One of the biggest strengths of this college is its teachers. I was fortunate to learn from supportive and dedicated teachers such as Sangeeta Ma'am and especially Melba Ma'am, who guided me tremendously in Mathematics. Their patience, teaching methods, and willingness to help students made a huge difference in my academic journey.

The college has experienced teachers for different subjects, each bringing their own teaching style and positive attitude to the classroom. Beyond academics, the college also organizes meaningful competitions and activities that help students develop confidence, skills, and memorable experiences.

My advice to future students is simple: attend lectures regularly, interact with your teachers, and don't hesitate to ask questions whenever you have doubts. The faculty is genuinely supportive and willing to help students who show interest in learning.

As for some of the negative reviews online, I believe many of them come from students who rarely attended lectures or had issues due to their own behavior and expectations. While everyone is entitled to their opinion, my personal experience was overwhelmingly positive

Our experience with Tolani College of Commerce (Junior College) has been extremely disappointing. No genuine academic or emotional support has been provided to the student. On the contrary, staff have used hand gestures ridiculing both parents and children, which is insulting and unprofessional.
As a parent, I too faced disrespect. Ms. Melba raised her voice and even demanded an apology from me when I raised valid concerns.

Such repeated patterns of bullying, ridicule, and poor communication highlight what feels like a substandard institution in terms of professionalism and values. Families expect empathy, dignity, and consistent support from educators — unfortunately, that has not been our experience at Tolani College of Commerce (Junior College).

Don’t ever send your child here

featured_reviews.review_text:
My Journey at M.L. Dahanukar College of Commerce

As a proud alumnus of Parle Tilak Vidyalaya Association's M.L. Dahanukar College of Commerce, I can confidently say that this institution has played a significant role in shaping who I am today—both professionally and personally. Nestled in the heart of Vile Parle (East), Mumbai, Dahanukar College stands as a symbol of academic excellence, discipline, and vibrant student life.

A Legacy of Excellence

Established in 1960, M.L. Dahanukar College has a rich legacy of over six decades in the field of commerce education. Named after the well-known industrialist and philanthropist Late Shri Madhavji Laxmidas Dahanukar, the college is managed by the reputed Parle Tilak Vidyalaya Association (PTVA). The institution has grown consistently, adapting to the changing educational landscape while staying grounded in its values.

Academics and Faculty

The college offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs, including B.Com, BMS, BAF, BBI, BFM, and M.Com. The faculty members are not only well-qualified but also deeply committed to student success. Their teaching style is a perfect blend of theory and real-world applications, making lectures both informative and engaging.

Vibrant Campus Life

One of my fondest memories is participating in college festivals like "Kurukshetra", which brought out the best in us—teamwork, creativity, leadership, and a sense of community. From cultural events to seminars and NSS/NCC activities, the college provides an ideal environment for all-round development.

Infrastructure and Support

The college has excellent infrastructure with well-equipped classrooms, a computer lab, a library with a vast collection of books and journals, and a student-friendly environment. The administrative staff is also very cooperative and supportive, making student life smooth and hassle-free.

Alumni Pride

As an alumnus, I always carry the values and lessons I learned here with great pride. M.L. Dahanukar is not just a college—it’s a place where careers are nurtured, confidence is built, and dreams are turned into reality. It has produced many successful professionals across fields like finance, management, education, entrepreneurship, and civil services.

Conclusion:
Looking back, I feel grateful to be a part of this institution. The knowledge, skills, and values I received here continue to guide me in my journey. If you’re looking for a college that offers academic strength, a supportive environment, and vibrant student life, M.L. Dahanukar College of Commerce is the place to be.

featured_reviews.review_text:
“A college that sells big promises but fails to deliver where it matters most.” That is the most accurate description of this institution.

I am writing this so future students do not get trapped by branding, glossy brochures, and admission-time promises.

During admissions, the Admissions Counselor told us things like, “We have 100% placements” and “We don’t even entertain companies offering below 6 LPA.” However, the actual placement outcomes tell a very different story. The reality is almost the opposite, companies offering below 6 LPA are entertained, while companies offering above 6 LPA rarely seem interested in the college.

The college heavily markets a highest package of 30 LPA, but what they don’t clearly tell you is that this was not a conventional fresh placement. The person was already working, pursued an MBA in Real Estate here, and then got that package. Presenting that as a standard placement benchmark for students is misleading.

Placements are one of the biggest disappointments. Corporate connections are close to zero. Students are pushed toward low-paying sales roles or irrelevant opportunities. Even roles as low as 3–3.5 LPA are presented as acceptable outcomes after paying around 10 lakhs in fees.

When students raised concerns about poor placements, the HOD/Placement Director responded with statements like:

* “Beggars can’t be choosers.”
* “At least get your foot in the door.”
* “Take any job now, even if it’s marketing/sales or unrelated, and switch later.”

Imagine paying premium fees for a specialized management degree only to be told to settle for anything.

If students reject irrelevant sales internships or jobs, the Placement Team often says: “We gave you opportunities, you didn’t take them.” But giving opportunities that students never wanted or that don’t align with their specialization is not meaningful placement support.

Another favorite line used to shift blame came from the HOD / Academic Leadership: “Students lack skills.”
If students truly lack employable skills, then what exactly are students paying nearly 10 lakhs for? Isn’t skill development supposed to be one of the institution’s core responsibilities?

Internship support is also weak. The college shows little genuine concern about whether students secure meaningful internships aligned with their career goals.

Batch size claims are also questionable. They claim around 30 students each for General MBA and Real Estate, but actual numbers often feel much lower, roughly 10–15 per batch.

Even university-level initiatives like career expos have been underwhelming. For the past 2 years, these events have failed to deliver what was promised. Big company names are advertised to attract students, registrations happen, and expectations are built, but many of those companies never actually show up. For example, students were told companies like Deloitte and Accenture would attend the career expo, but they did not arrive. There were several other companies as well that were advertised but never came. This creates false expectations and further damages trust.

Internal coordination among staff is poor. Communication gaps, lack of alignment, and weak execution are common.

Let me be clear: the infrastructure is good. The campus looks premium. But good infrastructure alone cannot justify such high fees.

Also, prospective students should not judge this college solely by the positive reviews here. This may be one of the few negative reviews you see, but that itself should make you question how much of the public perception reflects the actual student experience.

If you are choosing a college based on placements, corporate exposure, internship support, and career outcomes—please research thoroughly before investing your money here.
